resources.string: The map
Every page has a fixed place. Tap a place to see how it is reached.
A solid line is a drag in both directions. A dashed line is a page opened from a row; it can only be dragged back.
The middle of the map. Back always ends here, and four pages lie around it.
Above Home. Drag Home downwards to uncover it.
At the start side of Home. Drag Home towards the end side to uncover it.
Below Home. Drag Home upwards to uncover it.
At the end side of Home. Drag Home towards the start side to uncover it.
You are here, beyond Interactions. A row opened this page; drag it towards the end side to go back.
Try it
Go back to Home and move the pages with one finger.
Drag in each of the four directions. The page under the finger and the one it uncovers travel together, edge to edge.
Drag slowly, then reverse without lifting. The pages stay under the finger the whole way.
Let go before 28 % of the way and the page glides back. Let go after it and the new page lands.
Flick. A quick, short stroke lands the new page as well.
Measured here: drag this page back towards %1$s
At rest. Nothing is moving.
%1$d %% of the way to %2$s. Letting go now glides back.
%1$d %% of the way to %2$s. Letting go now lands there.
Another activity as a neighbour
A second activity can arrive and leave like a page of the map.
The button starts a separate activity. It glides in from the end side over a picture of this screen, and it can be dragged back out or left with system back.
Open the neighbour
System back

On Android 14 and later, the back gesture previews the move: this page follows the swipe part of the way towards the page it came from. Completing the gesture lands there, and cancelling it glides back.
Back to %1$s

Extracted from the original app: both pages travelling together, the 28 % and flick rules, and the activity that behaves like a neighbour. New in Sancai: a graph that describes any app, listeners and right-to-left.
